# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a section's when the game first draws with its shaders,
# so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's
# docs/porting.md, Prebuilt shader lists).
# Recorded by code, not by playing: bash tools/record_shaders.sh (its header says how) runs N64Recomp-browser's
# tools/record_shaders.mjs with tools/shader_plan.json, which loads the page fresh for each section. Section 0 is the
# launcher, the logos, the title, the file select, the mode select and a Battle Royale's setup, reached as
# tools/play_plan.json reaches them. Then a section a board, the Battle Royale map's six, each started from the setup
# with the board's index written where the setup reads it (GwSystem's current_board_index, 0x800CD059) and played by
# the computer for a minute and a half, Chilly Waters for a whole turn: the minigame's instructions, the minigame the
# board picks, its results and back to the board. Then the 70 minigames, six a section: the survey (patches/survey.c,
# tools/survey.js) takes the setup's way to the first board to the first minigame instead, and each minigame's end to
# the next, with the teams its kind has (1 vs 3, 2 vs 2, 4 players, one player) and four computer players, who play
# each to its end but the last, Dizzy Dinghies, which they don't finish in the three minutes it is played. Not
# recorded: the Duel Map and its boards, Story mode, the Mini-Game House, the options and the records. One shader is
# added by hand to section 0: a board's start missed it in plays from a 3840x2000 canvas. Flags follow settings
# (filtering, HDR, MSAA, upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means recording again.
